日文.首段: 京阪70型電車（けいはん70がたでんしゃ）は、かつて京阪電気鉄道の京津線で使用されていた電車（路面電車車両）である。

章节.概要:
もともと、1940年（昭和15年）に無蓋貨車3101・02を大津線用固定クロスシート付オープンカー（制御車）に改造し、その牽引車となる予定であった車両である。100型の車体を50型に準じた新製車体に載せ替えたもので、70 - 79の10両が製造された。戦局を鑑みて資材・資金を節減した改造車であったが、車体長は50型よりも1m長く、車体幅も同形式と比較して10mm広い。

1943年（昭和18年）4月に守口工場で75が竣工し、続いて同年12月に73が竣工した。残る8両は戦時下の資材不足により半鋼製車体が製造されたのみで完成できず、戦後の1948年（昭和23年）に東洋機械興業により竣工した。 しかし、同年10月30日、京津線蹴上 - 九条山間にて発生した浜大津行き電車のポール外れを発端とする後退リレー衝突事故により72が損傷し、東洋機械興業へ再入場した。
さらに、1949年（昭和24年）8月7日に発生した京津線四宮車庫の火災により72を除く9両が被災し、翌1950年（昭和25年）1月31日付けで廃車された。72は火災発生当時、前述した事故による復旧のため東洋機械興業で修理中だったおかげで偶然にも難を逃れたのであった。
残った72は1967年（昭和42年）まで京津線で使用され、80型の増備によって車籍からは抹消されたが、守口工場の牽引車として使用することになり、1968年（昭和43年）に連結器取付と集電装置のトロリーポールをパンタグラフへ交換、外部色を茶色・正面警戒色にした。1970年（昭和45年）には外部色の茶色をフタリットブルーに変更している。

守口工場から寝屋川車両基地への移転後も構内入換車として使用され、運転席の脇の扉とステップなど木造部品が残っている。この移転後の1983年（昭和58年）に以下の改修を受けている。
架線電圧1500V昇圧に伴う工事として車内に複電圧の電動発電機を搭載した。自走用主電動機の電源もこの電動発電機で発電する交流200Vを使用し、変圧器と整流器を通して直流600Vに変換している。
車体更新を実施し、正面の前照灯を屋上から窓下の埋め込みに変更した。側面の窓を一部撤去し、残存側窓のHゴム化と通風用グリルを設置し、川側の側面に大型扉を設けた。
なお、台車と主電動機は元をたどると京阪創業当時の1型のもので、1910年（明治43年）の製造から100年以上にわたり現役で使用されていることになる。
2014年9月、寝屋川車両基地で進められていた60型（びわこ号）修復プロジェクトにおいて構内で60型を牽引することが発表され、「ワガヤネヤガワ号」という愛称が新たに付された。車番「72」を復元し、側窓を描いた板を設置して上半クリーム・下半ライトブルーに塗装変更している。2014年11月9日の「びわこ号復活記念乗車会」では事前の告知通りに寝屋川車両基地構内で60型電車を牽引・推進した。ただし、車体すべてが現役当時の仕様で復元されたものではない。

中文.首段: 京阪70型电力动车组（けいはん70がたでんしゃ）是过去在京阪电气铁道京津线上使用的电力动车组（有轨电车车辆）。

章节.概要:
该车原本是1940年（昭和15年）将无盖货车3101、02改造为大津线用带固定交叉座椅的敞篷车（控制车），并预定作为其牵引车的车辆。它是将100型车体换装到准照50型的新造车体上，共制造了70～79的10辆。考虑到战局，这是节省资材与资金的改造车，但车体长度比50型长1 m，车体宽度也比同型宽10 mm。
1943年（昭和18年）4月，75在守口工厂竣工，接着同年12月73竣工。剩余8辆因战时资材不足，仅制造出半钢制车体而未能完成，战后1948年（昭和23年）由东洋机械兴业竣工。然而，同年10月30日，京津线蹴上～九条山间发生以开往滨大津电车集电杆脱落为起因的后退继电器冲撞事故，72受损，再次入厂东洋机械兴业。
此外，1949年（昭和24年）8月7日发生的京津线四宫车库火灾使除72外的9辆受灾，并于翌1950年（昭和25年）1月31日办理报废。72在火灾发生时因前述事故正在东洋机械兴业修理以进行修复，从而偶然幸免于难。
残存的72在京津线使用至1967年（昭和42年），随着80型的增备而从车籍中注销，但决定作为守口工厂的牵引车使用，1968年（昭和43年）加装车钩，并将集电装置的集电杆更换为受电弓，外部涂色改为茶色、正面警戒色。1970年（昭和45年）将外部涂色的茶色改为Futarit Blue。
从守口工厂转移至寝屋川车辆基地后，仍作为场内调车车使用，驾驶席旁的车门与踏板等木制部件仍然保留。转移后的1983年（昭和58年）接受了以下改修。
作为伴随架线电压1500V升压的工程，在车内搭载了复电压电动发电机。自走用主电动机的电源也使用该电动发电机发出的交流200V，通过变压器与整流器转换为直流600V。
实施了车体更新，将正面的前照灯从车顶改为窗下的嵌入式。拆除部分侧面车窗，将残存侧窗改为H橡胶并设置通风格栅，在河侧侧面设置大型车门。
另外，转向架与主电动机追溯起源是京阪创业当时1型的，从1910年（明治43年）制造起已现役使用100年以上。
2014年9月，在寝屋川车辆基地推进的60型（琵琶湖号）修复项目中，宣布将在场内牵引60型，并被新命名为“ワガヤネヤガワ号”这一爱称。复原了车号“72”，设置画有侧窗的板，涂装变更为上半奶油色、下半浅蓝色。在2014年11月9日的“琵琶湖号复活纪念乘车会”上，如事先告知那样在寝屋川车辆基地场内牵引、推进了60型电车。不过，并非整个车体都按现役当时的规格复原。

英文.首段: The Keihan 70 series (けいはん70がたでんしゃ) is an electric tramcar (streetcar) that was formerly used on the Keishin Line of Keihan Electric Railway.

章节.Overview:
It was originally a vehicle that, in 1940 (Showa 15), was planned to be the towing car for the open cars (control cars) with fixed cross seats for the Otsu Line, which were created by rebuilding open wagons 3101 and 02. It was made by mounting the body of the 100 series onto a newly built body modeled on the 50 series, and ten cars, 70 to 79, were built. In view of the war situation it was a rebuilt car that saved materials and funds, but its body length was 1 m longer than the 50 series and its body width was 10 mm wider than that type.
In April 1943 (Showa 18), 75 was completed at the Moriguchi Works, and then in December of the same year 73 was completed. The remaining eight cars could not be finished because only semi-steel bodies were built due to wartime material shortages, and they were completed in 1948 (Showa 23) after the war by Toyo Kikai Kogyo. However, on October 30 of the same year, 72 was damaged in a rear-end relay collision accident triggered by a trolley pole coming off a train bound for Hamaotsu between Keishin Line's Keage and Kuzuyama, and it re-entered Toyo Kikai Kogyo.
Furthermore, in the fire at the Keishin Line's Shinomiya Depot on August 7, 1949 (Showa 24), nine cars other than 72 were affected and were scrapped as of January 31 of the following year, 1950 (Showa 25). At the time of the fire, 72 happened to escape harm because it was under repair at Toyo Kikai Kogyo to be restored from the aforementioned accident.
The surviving 72 was used on the Keishin Line until 1967 (Showa 42) and was removed from the register with the addition of the 80 series, but it was decided to use it as a towing car at the Moriguchi Works; in 1968 (Showa 43) a coupler was fitted and its trolley pole current collector was replaced with a pantograph, and its exterior color was changed to brown with a warning color on the front. In 1970 (Showa 45) the brown exterior color was changed to Futarit Blue.
After the move from the Moriguchi Works to the Neyagawa Depot, it continued to be used as a yard shunting car, and wooden parts such as the door beside the driver's seat and the step remain. After this move, in 1983 (Showa 58) it underwent the following modifications.
As work accompanying the increase of the overhead line voltage to 1500 V, a dual-voltage motor-generator was installed in the car. The power for the self-propelling traction motors also used the AC 200 V generated by this motor-generator, converted to DC 600 V through a transformer and rectifier.
The body was renewed, and the front headlight was changed from the roof to a recessed type below the window. Some side windows were removed, the remaining side windows were fitted with H-rubber and ventilation grilles were installed, and a large door was provided on the river-side face.
Incidentally, the bogies and traction motors trace back to those of the Type 1 of Keihan's founding era, meaning they have been in active service for over 100 years since their manufacture in 1910 (Meiji 43).
In September 2014, in the 60 series (Biwako-go) restoration project being carried out at the Neyagawa Depot, it was announced that it would tow the 60 series within the yard, and it was newly given the nickname "Wagaya Neyagawa-go." Car number "72" was restored, a board depicting the side windows was installed, and the livery was changed to cream on the upper half and light blue on the lower half. At the "Biwako-go Revival Commemorative Ride" on November 9, 2014, as previously announced, it towed and pushed the 60 series car within the Neyagawa Depot yard. However, not the entire body was restored to its specifications when in service.

== Overview ==
It was originally a vehicle that, in 1940 (Showa 15), was planned to be the towing car for the open cars (control cars) with fixed cross seats for the Otsu Line, which were created by rebuilding open wagons 3101 and 02. It was made by mounting the body of the 100 series onto a newly built body modeled on the 50 series, and ten cars, 70 to 79, were built. In view of the war situation it was a rebuilt car that saved materials and funds, but its body length was 1 m longer than the 50 series and its body width was 10 mm wider than that type.
In April 1943 (Showa 18), 75 was completed at the Moriguchi Works, and then in December of the same year 73 was completed. The remaining eight cars could not be finished because only semi-steel bodies were built due to wartime material shortages, and they were completed in 1948 (Showa 23) after the war by Toyo Kikai Kogyo. However, on October 30 of the same year, 72 was damaged in a rear-end relay collision accident triggered by a trolley pole coming off a train bound for Hamaotsu between Keishin Line's Keage and Kuzuyama, and it re-entered Toyo Kikai Kogyo.
Furthermore, in the fire at the Keishin Line's Shinomiya Depot on August 7, 1949 (Showa 24), nine cars other than 72 were affected and were scrapped as of January 31 of the following year, 1950 (Showa 25). At the time of the fire, 72 happened to escape harm because it was under repair at Toyo Kikai Kogyo to be restored from the aforementioned accident.
The surviving 72 was used on the Keishin Line until 1967 (Showa 42) and was removed from the register with the addition of the 80 series, but it was decided to use it as a towing car at the Moriguchi Works; in 1968 (Showa 43) a coupler was fitted and its trolley pole current collector was replaced with a pantograph, and its exterior color was changed to brown with a warning color on the front. In 1970 (Showa 45) the brown exterior color was changed to Futarit Blue.
